newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends down in thin pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends down in thin pre-holiday trade.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended lower on Thursday in quiet dealings ahead of the long weekend in the U.S.
Benchmark Setpember futures fell 4.00 cents a lb, to end at 168.35, after trading from 167.50 to 174 cents. Spot July ended down 8.50 cents, while the outer months closed down 1.00 to up 1.50 cents.
Traders said the absence of a crop-damaging freeze in top-grower Brazil has weighed on the market in recent days.

Predictions of a cold front had sparked a round of nervous buying early in the week, but the market quickly retreated once forecasters said temperatures would remain above freezing levels in the coffee belt.

Traders also noted the potential for a large build-up in the exchange's certified inventories. Stocks rose by 725 60-kg bags as of July 2, to 50,550 bags, the CSCE said after the close of business on Thursday, but an additional 37,295 bags were pending exchange approval.
While there is no guarantee that the coffee will meet CSCE grading specifications, traders said they expected at least some of the coffee to be certified.
An estimated 4,559 lots were exchanged on the day.
The CSCE will be closed on Friday, July 4, in observance of Independence Day.
